I found one minor edge-case regression and no definite bugs. The uncommitted change is in `bash_completionsV2.go`, in `__%[1]s_handle_standard_completion_case`, around line 194. It replaces the `compgen -W "$comp" -- "$cur"` filter with the literal prefix test `[[ $comp == "$cur"* ]] || continue`.

**Minor regression: empty completions are no longer skipped (line 194)**
- The old code ran `[[ -z $comp ]] && continue`, which dropped any line whose completion text was empty. That covered a description-only line such as `\tsome description`.
- The new test matches an empty `$comp` whenever `$cur` is empty, which is the case when the user hits TAB on an empty word.
- The empty entry is then added to `COMPREPLY`. It also counts toward the `-eq 1` single-completion check, and it goes through description formatting.
- Cobra normally doesn't emit such lines, so this is unlikely in practice. Adding `[[ -n $comp ]] &&` to the test restores the old behavior.

**Behavior changes that look intentional or harmless**
- The old code re-expanded `$comp` through `compgen -W`. That caused word splitting and expansion of special characters in completions, and it changed the value used to compute `longest`. The new literal prefix match avoids this and is arguably a fix.
- `==` matching honors `shopt -s nocasematch`, whereas `compgen` didn't. This only matters for users who have that option set.

I only read the diff and the surrounding function. I didn't run any shell tests.
